interest: This file offers a fascinating glimpse into the early era of transpacific radio broadcasting and public diplomacy between the United States and Japan during the interwar period. It illustrates the meticulous attention State Department officials paid to diplomatic reciprocity and protocol, strictly calibrating official U.S. representation to match Japan's and withholding the Secretary of State once Foreign Minister Kōki Hirota withdrew in favor of Prince Iesato Tokugawa. Furthermore, it reveals the pivotal role of commercial broadcasters like NBC and private civic groups like the Japan Society of New York as diplomatic intermediaries capable of maintaining international goodwill when formal governmental participation was constrained.
overview: This file (decimal file 894.46 / File 577, titled 'Entertainment in Japan') documents diplomatic protocol deliberations surrounding a proposed joint American-Japanese international radio broadcast for the Fourth of July in 1934. Coordinated by the National Broadcasting Company (NBC) through its Washington representative K. H. Berkeley and the Japanese Broadcasting Company, the program was planned to include musical entertainment alongside goodwill messages from prominent figures in both nations. The initial proposal contemplated addresses by Japanese Foreign Minister Kōki Hirota, U.S. Ambassador Joseph C. Grew, and Secretary of State Cordell Hull. However, internal State Department discussions led by James Clement Dunn addressed sensitive protocol questions regarding whether Secretary Hull should speak in person or via surrogate, contingent upon Hirota's direct participation. When NBC subsequently reported that Hirota would not participate and that Prince Iesato Tokugawa had been substituted in a private capacity, the State Department concurred that official U.S. governmental participation should likewise be withdrawn in favor of prominent private citizens affiliated with Japanese-American affairs, specifically Henry W. Taft, President of the Japan Society of New York, or former Under Secretary of State William R. Castle.

subfiles.about: Informs the State Department of a planned July 4th international broadcast arranged with the Japanese Broadcasting Company and requests a State Department speaker.
subfiles.summary: K. H. Berkeley of the National Broadcasting Company's Washington office informs the State Department's Division of Far Eastern Affairs that the Japanese Broadcasting Company has arranged a special Fourth of July broadcast featuring messages from Japanese Foreign Minister Kōki Hirota and U.S. Ambassador Joseph C. Grew. NBC arranged an accompanying musical program preceding the Japanese broadcast and requests that an official from the State Department deliver a brief address appropriate to the occasion. The entry includes a cross-reference to file 111.018.
subfiles.title: NBC Request for State Department Speaker for July 4th Broadcast
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (FE: PC), Department of State

subfiles.about: Discusses NBC's request for Secretary of State Cordell Hull to deliver a talk for the July 4th international radio broadcast.
subfiles.from: James Clement Dunn, Department of State
subfiles.summary: James Clement Dunn discusses the request from the National Broadcasting Company for the Secretary of State to deliver a short talk during the special July 4th broadcast to Japan. The memorandum considers the potential subject matter and weighs whether Secretary Hull should speak in person, have a prepared message read by a surrogate, or designate another official to deliver the talk. Dunn notes that he requested NBC representative K. H. Berkeley to determine definitively whether Foreign Minister Hirota will speak in person.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Dunn on Proposed Secretary of State Talk for July 4th Broadcast

subfiles.about: Reports the substitution of Prince Tokugawa for Foreign Minister Hirota and approves selecting non-official American speakers for the broadcast.
subfiles.from: James Clement Dunn, Department of State
subfiles.summary: James Clement Dunn records a telephone message from K. H. Berkeley of NBC reporting that Foreign Minister Hirota will not speak on the July 4th broadcast and that Prince Iesato Tokugawa has been substituted on the program. Because Prince Tokugawa was not appearing in an official government capacity, NBC sought to invite a prominent private American figure with Japanese ties, specifically Henry W. Taft (President of the Japan Society of New York) or former Under Secretary William R. Castle. Dunn confirmed that this non-official arrangement would be appropriate under the circumstances.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Dunn on Substitution of Prince Tokugawa and Non-Official American Speakers
